# heist_application (Data Source)

Looks up one application by ID or URL, including applications Heist discovered and ones created outside Terraform.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# Look up an application Heist discovered by its URL.
data "heist_application" "api" {
  url = "https://api.example.com"
}

output "api" {
  value = {
    id              = data.heist_application.api.id
    in_scope        = data.heist_application.api.in_scope
    requires_review = data.heist_application.api.requires_review
  }
}

# Look up an application by ID.
data "heist_application" "by_id" {
  id = "00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000000"
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Optional

- `id` (String) Application ID to look up. Exactly one of `id` and `url` is required.
- `url` (String) Application URL to look up. Exactly one of `id` and `url` is required. Matching ignores scheme and host case and a trailing slash, and fails unless exactly one application matches.

### Read-Only

- `created_at` (String) When the application was created.
- `domain` (String) Workspace domain the application belongs to, for example `example.com` for `app.example.com`.
- `environment` (String) Environment of the application, or null when unset.
- `git_repository` (Attributes) Git repository attached to the application, or null when none is. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--git_repository))
- `in_scope` (Boolean) Whether Heist tests the application.
- `main_target` (Boolean) Whether the application is a main target rather than one discovered by Heist.
- `missing_auth` (Boolean) Whether the application needs authentication Heist does not have.
- `parent_application_ids` (List of String) IDs of the applications this one was discovered under. Empty for root applications.
- `requires_review` (Boolean) Whether the application needs review in Heist.

<a id="nestedatt--git_repository"></a>
### Nested Schema for `git_repository`

Read-Only:

- `name` (String) Repository name.
- `owner` (String) Repository owner or organization.
- `project` (String) Project containing the repository, or null when the provider has none.
- `provider` (String) Git hosting provider.
